questions.question:
**Choose the option that is the correct direct form of the sentence.**

She said that she would not be coming to the school that day.

options.text: She had said "She must not be coming to the school today".
She said, "You will not be coming to the school today".
She said, "I may not come to the school tomorrow."
She said, "I will not be coming to the school today".

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **She said, "I will not be coming to the school today".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Indirect Speech. As per the question we have to change it into Direct Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• **'Said'** will remain unchanged.
 
• Comma and inverted commas will be added. 
 
• '**would**' will be changed into 'will'. 
 
• 'she' will be changed into 'I'.
 
• **'that day'** changes to '**today**'.
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4. 

 
 
 

Correct Sentence:__ *She said, "I will not be coming to the school today".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The following table will enable us to know how tense changes in indirect speech:-

 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object)
 Simple Past (Subject + V2 + Object)
 
 

 Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object)
 Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object)
 
 

 Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 + Object)
 Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object)
 
 

 Simple Past (Subject + V2 + Object)
 Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object)
 
 

 Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object)
 Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object)
 
 

 Simple Future (Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object)
 Present Conditional (Subject + would + V1 +Object)
 
 

 Future Continuous (Subject + will/shall + V1 + ing + Object)
 Conditional Continuous (Subject + would + be + V1 + ing + Object)

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

They said that they would issue the certificate the following week

options.text: They said, “They are issuing the certificate the next week.”
They said, “We will issue the certificate next week.”
They said, “Could we issue the certificate the following week?”
They said, “They issued the certificate the following week.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Whenever we convert indirect speech to direct speech, it's important to remember the following points:
 
 
• The conjunction **"That" **should be changed into inverted commas(," ")
 
• Make changes in the **reported speech clause** according to the type of sentence.
 
• Change time and place references like "**that day**" into "**today**", "**the day before**" into "**yesterday**", "**the following week**" into "**next week**", etc.
 
• For example: 
 
 
• He said that he lived in Delhi. (Indirect)
 
• *He said, "I live in Delhi. (direct)*
 
• She said that she would call me the following day. (indirect)
 
• *She said, " I will call you tomorrow. (direct)*
 
 
 
 

Based on the above points & examples, the correct sentence should be "*They said, "We will issue the certificate next week"*.

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct narration of the given sentence.**

Madhav applauded her, saying that she had done well.

options.text: Madhav say, “Bravo! You have done well”.
Madhav said, “Bravo! You have done well”.
Madhav said, “Bravo! You been done well”.
Madhav say, “Bravo! You have be done well”.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Madhav said, “Bravo! You have done well”.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in indirect speech.
 
• In direct speech, the reporting verb "**saying**" is changed to "**said**" and the tense of the verb "**had done**" is changed to "**have done**".
 
• The sentence also includes an **exclamation**, which is retained in the direct narration.
 
• Therefore, the correct direct narration is "*Madhav said, 'Bravo! You have done well*'".

Hence, **option 2** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because it uses "say" instead of "said".
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because it uses "been done" instead of "have done".
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because it uses "be done" instead of "have done".

__
 
• To convert the given sentence into **direct speech**, '**that**' should be removed.
 
• The **statement **should be quoted in **inverted commas**.
 
• As we know when the **reporting speech **(*Netra says*) is in the **present tense**, there will be **no changes **in the **reported speech**.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct direct form of the sentence.

Shubham said that his father was playing cricket with him.

options.text: Shubham said, “My father was playing cricket with me.”
Shubham said, “My father is playing cricket with me.”
Shubham said, “My father played cricket with me.”
Shubham said, “My father had played cricket with me.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **The original sentence** states that Shubham said that his father** "was"** playing cricket with him.
 
• **When we convert** direct speech to indirect speech, we generally need to shift the verb tense back one step.
 
• However, in this case, option 2** maintains the present tense of the verb** "is" because it accurately reflects the original sentence's meaning.

Therefore, the** correct sentence **is: *'Shubham said, “My father is playing cricket with me.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1)** "Shubham said, 'My father was playing cricket with me.'" changes the verb tense to **past tense ("was playing"), **which does not align with the reported speech. The original sentence indicates that the father is currently playing cricket, so the present tense should be maintained.
 
• **Option 3)** "Shubham said, 'My father played cricket with me.'" changes the verb tense to **past tense ("played"),** which again does not accurately convey the present ongoing action of the father playing cricket.
 
• **Option 4)** "Shubham said, 'My father had played cricket with me.'" uses the **past perfect tense ("had played"),** which suggests an action completed before a past point of reference. However, there is no specific past point of reference mentioned in the original sentence, so the past perfect tense is not necessary.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence indirect speech.**

The customer asked the bank manager if they were working on the following Saturday

options.text: The customer asked the bank manager, “Are they working on the previous Saturday?”
The customer asks the bank manager, “If you were working on the following Saturday?”
The customer said to the bank manager, “Are you working next Saturday?”
The customer said to the bank manager, “Were they working on the previous Saturday?”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is*** *'The customer said to the bank manager, “Are you working next Saturday?”'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in Indirect speech.
 
• As the given sentence has 'if' it means the interrogative reported speech will be there in Direct speech.
 
• The pronoun will be used according to the object that is 'Bank manager' so the pronoun will be 'You'
 
• The tense will be the present continuous tense.
 
• The reporting verb 'asked' will be changed into 'said to'.

**So the correct answer is-*** The customer said to the bank manager, “Are you working next Saturday?”*

questions.question:
**Select the option that is the direct form of the sentence.**

The doctor advised Jaya to put the eye drops into her eyes four times a day from the next day.

options.text: The doctor advised Jaya, “From tomorrow put the eye drops into her eyes four times a day.”
The doctor advises Jaya, “From the next day put the eye drops into your eyes four times a day.”
The doctor advised Jaya, “From tomorrow put the eye drops into your eyes four times a day.”
The doctor had advised Jaya, “From the next day you put the eye drops into your eyes four times a day.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The doctor advised Jaya, “From tomorrow put the eye drops into your eyes four times a day.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from indirect to direct speech:
 
• When the indirect speech is in an assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• Change the sentence in the direct speech from assertive to imperative.
 
• The tense of reported speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense. 
 
• The reporting verb 'advised' will remain the same.
 
• 'To infinitive' is replaced by a comma and inverted commas.
 
• ​Words showing time and place are changed accordingly. (the next day - tomorrow)
 
• ​​The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
 
 
• Here 'her' will be converted into 'your' as per the subject.
 
 
 
• 'to put' changes into 'put'.
 
 
 
• At last line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we finally get-* The doctor advised Jaya, “From tomorrow put the eye drops into your eyes four times a day.”*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• The sentence which expresses a prayer, keen wish, curse, etc. is called an optative sentence.
 
• This kind of sentence generally starts with 'may' and 'wish'.
